cards.text: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus shows Himself to His disciples again. Seven of them are together: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples.

cards.question: The disciples are together by the sea. Simon Peter tells the others what he's going to do. What is it?
The others tell Peter they'll go with him. They get into the boat and stay out all night. How does the night go?

answers.text: They catch a few small fish

cards.text: After a whole night of nothing, early in the morning Jesus is standing on the shore, but the disciples don't recognize that it's Him. I've stared at dough that wouldn't rise till the sun came up, friend, so believe me, I FEEL that boat.

cards.question: The disciples don't know it's Jesus on the shore. He calls out to them in the boat. What does He ask?

answers.text: If He can use their boat

cards.question: The disciples tell the Man on the shore they have no fish. So He tells them to cast the net on the ___ side of the boat, and they'll find some.
The disciples cast the net right where the Man on the shore says. What happens when they try to haul it in?

answers.text: They can't with so many fish

cards.text: ALL NIGHT with nothing, then one word from the shore and they can't even pull the net in! That's me burning batch after batch until midnight, then somebody leans in, says one thing, and suddenly I'm out of TRAYS.

cards.question: The net is too full to haul in. Then the disciple whom Jesus loved turns to Peter and says something. What does he say?
As soon as Simon Peter hears that the Man on the shore is the Lord, he stays put in the boat to help with the net.

cards.text: Peter puts his outer garment back on, since he'd taken it off, and jumps into the sea. The man got DRESSED to go swimming, and friend, I respect it.

cards.question: Peter's in the water. The other disciples come ashore in the boat, dragging the net full of fish. How far from land are they?

cards.text: When they land, there's a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread. That's like dragging yourself into the bakery before sunrise and the oven's already warm, a batch already cooling, and you didn't do a THING.

cards.question: Jesus already has fish on the fire. What does He tell the disciples to bring?

answers.text: Some of the fish they just caught

cards.question: Simon Peter goes aboard and drags the net ashore. It's full of large fish. How many?
With so many large fish in it, the disciples' net tears.

cards.text: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus says to them. Not one disciple dares to ask Him who He is, and they all know it's the Lord.

cards.question: Breakfast by the fire is ready. Who comes and hands the bread and the fish to the disciples?
This breakfast by the sea was now the ___ time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.

cards.text: Breakfast by the fire, the net still full on the shore, and that's where we'll pause. Trust me, friend, this morning by the sea isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 9 of the 13 choice cards. True or false and fill in the blank have only 2 each, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The passage opens with "Later," which is mid-story. The opening card never says this happens after Jesus was raised from the dead, so the baker doesn't know what "again" refers to. It can say He has risen without giving away the count asked on card 19.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This is the first time the sons of Zebedee show up, and the card doesn't say simply who they are: James and John (Matthew 4:21), with the reference.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks which side of the boat (right, left or front). That is wording the baker hasn't seen and can't reason out from earlier cards. It's pure luck, and the blank doesn't test meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only retells verse 6, which card 7 already covered, and adds a joke. It doesn't carry the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The story-continues line closely copies the doc's example ("that's where we'll..." / "Trust me, friend, this ... not done/finished yet") instead of being newly written. "This morning by the sea isn't finished yet" also hints that the next passage happens at the same breakfast.

rule.text: If the passage is in a story group and isn't the last passage in it, the last story card ends with a short line from Papa Dorin saying the story isn't over (or the teaching isn't done). It gives nothing away about what happens next. The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
